subject: Post-call recap: audit log filtering & PII handling scope (HealthFirst)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy.liu@healthfirst.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap: audit log filtering & PII handling scope (HealthFirst)

Amy — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the asks you had so we can align on next steps.

Key points from the call:
- Primary concern: request/response audit logs currently include headers with trace IDs and some customer PII in nested JSON (customer_email, phone).
- HealthFirst needs: (1) ability to prevent storage of raw PII in logs; (2) configurable retention by data class and region (US-only for PHI-adjacent fields); (3) an audit trail showing what redaction rules were applied per request.

What Redwood can do (high-level):
- Per-endpoint sanitization rules: strip/mask specific headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie) and obfuscate trace IDs unless explicitly whitelisted.
- Request/response field mapping where customers provide a data map and we apply either masking (partial token), hash, or drop.
- Retention policies tied to data class + region: retention windows and exportable audit logs for compliance.

Open questions we need answers to from HealthFirst to scope a pilot:
1) Do you consider trace IDs themselves sensitive if they can be correlated to an internal user ID?
2) Which fields in the request/response payloads must be treated as PHI vs. non-PHI? Can you share a sample (PII redacted) or the data map?
3) What retention windows are required for audit logs and for sanitized copies separately?

Next steps we agreed on:
- Amy to share a redacted sample payload and the minimal data map (by EOD Wed, 11/18).
- Redwood to send a short proposal (sanitization approach + pilot timelines + required artifacts) by Thu 11/19.
- Schedule a 30-min technical walk-through with your security engineer after we receive the data map.

Attachments: healthfirst_data-map-template.xlsx (template for mapping fields) and a short PDF overview of our sanitization model.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample so we can size the pilot.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales (East) | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 617-555-0149
From: Amy Liu <amy.liu@healthfirst.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthfirst.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: audit log filtering & PII handling scope (HealthFirst)

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Trace IDs: we treat trace IDs as sensitive if they can be joined to user identifiers in our systems. We would prefer them hashed before being stored in any logs unless there's a business reason to keep a readable trace.
- Data map: I'll load a redacted sample into the template. Expect the file to include fields labeled as PHI (patient_name, patient_dob, ssn_partial), low-risk identifiers (device_id, locale), and call-level metadata (latency_ms, model_id).
- Retention: baseline requirement is 90 days for full audit records; sanitized/aggregated telemetry can be retained for up to 2 years. For PHI fields we want a separate retention policy that results in their removal from logs after 30 days unless a legal hold is asserted.

One request: can Redwood provide a per-request audit record that shows what rule was applied (mask/hash/drop) and a hash of the original value so we can reconcile when necessary? We don't need the original value in Redwood, just the ability to prove what happened.

I'll upload the template by 11/18 and loop in our security engineer for the walkthrough.

— Amy Liu
Director, Security and Compliance | HealthFirst Medical Group
amy.liu@healthfirst.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy.liu@healthfirst.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: audit log filtering & PII handling scope (HealthFirst)

Amy — thanks for the answers, that's super helpful. Quick notes from a product/engineering POV based on your asks: 

- Hashing trace IDs: we can support salted hashing per-customer so stored values are deterministic for your account but opaque otherwise. We'll include the salt in your KMS-protected configuration so only HealthFirst can compute/verifiy outside Redwood.
- Per-request audit record: we can emit a compact audit event that records the rule id applied and an HMAC of the original value (computed client-side or via a customer-managed key) so Redwood never stores the raw PII. That satisfies our current compliance gating for many customers.
- Retention tiers: we'll propose two layers — a 90-day raw-ish audit tier (with PII removed/hashed as you requested) and a long-term telemetry tier for aggregated metrics. We can put exact retention windows into the pilot SOW.

I'll draft the proposal this afternoon and add a short section on the audit event schema and the sanitization rule lifecycle (create, version, revoke).

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Amy Liu <amy.liu@healthfirst.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: audit log filtering & PII handling scope (HealthFirst)

Ben — that approach sounds good. A couple of small asks before we sign off on the pilot SOW:

1) Include an explicit rollback/forensic path: if HealthFirst needs an investigator to re-hydrate a masked value for an incident, what is the procedure and who approves it?
2) Can Redwood provide evidence from an existing customer (anonymized) that the audit-event approach has been used for reconciliation?

I'll upload the redacted data map by EOD and propose two time slots next week for the technical walkthrough. If you can include the proposed SLA targets for redaction latency (e.g., redaction must happen inline within X ms), please add that to the SOW.

Thanks — Amy
